title: Household fraud burden subgroup patterns vary across annual SHED samples
source_unit: Separate weighted US adult SHED annual respondent samples

denominator.unit: SHED public-use adult respondent rows; conditional outcomes use non-credit-card fraud reporters

observations.method: Codebook-backed BK47_b, BK48, BK50, ppagect4, and ppinc7 weighted with the main weight; metric-specific nonmissing denominators.
observations.uncertainty: Annual descriptive survey estimates without reproduced replicate-weight variance; self-report, nonresponse, and selection remain relevant.
observations.counterinterpretation: The subgroup ordering can reflect composition, reporting, fraud type, and resources rather than an age or income causal effect.

denominator.unit: SHED public-use adult respondent rows; conditional outcomes use non-credit-card fraud reporters

observations.method: Same definitions and weighted procedure applied to the 2025 public-use CSV.
observations.uncertainty: Annual descriptive survey estimates without reproduced replicate-weight variance; separate sample, not a panel.
observations.counterinterpretation: The changed age ordering does not establish a population trend; survey composition and coding or reporting differences may contribute.

related_sources.claim: Local reproduction output preserves annual subgroup measures and available-field differences.
related_sources.access_boundary: 2025 lacks the account-route fields used in the 2024 P2P comparison.

boundary: This adds a separate annual comparison to household fraud exposure and recovery burden. It does not establish a panel trend, causal subgroup effect, verified provider remedy, digital-access or disability gradient, later trust, switching, or exit.
